subject: FastRetail: Post-incident RCA, corrective actions, and follow-through
body:
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@fastretail.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: FastRetail SRE Team <sre@fastretail.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Production latency spike and errors impacting checkout - immediate attention

Markus —

We started seeing a sustained latency spike and elevated 5xx rates on the checkout route at ~08:45 PST. Peak p95 jumped to ~1.8s, and our customers are reporting failed carts. We escalated to our SREs but wanted Redwood on the thread given the recent model rollout.

Can someone confirm if there was a model variant or routing change in that window? We need a timeline and mitigation plan — this is impacting revenue.

Thanks,
Daniel
FastRetail, Sr. Engineering Manager

---

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@fastretail.com>
Cc: FastRetail SRE Team <sre@fastretail.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Nov 2027 09:29:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Production latency spike and errors impacting checkout - immediate attention

Daniel — thanks for flagging.

Quick notes while we dig in:
- I’m pulling the rollout/traffic routing logs for the checkout model.
- Rishi: please confirm whether any canary/full rollout or kernel swap occurred 08:30–09:00 PST.
- Kimberly: work with FastRetail SREs to put a temporary routing rule that pins traffic to the previous model family if we see degraded tail latency.

I’ll follow up in 15 with an initial readout.

–Markus
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

---

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: FastRetail SRE Team <sre@fastretail.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Nov 2027 09:36:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Production latency spike and errors impacting checkout - immediate attention

On Wed, Nov 3, 2027 at 9:29 AM Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com> wrote:
> Rishi: please confirm whether any canary/full rollout or kernel swap occurred 08:30–09:00 PST.

Checked rollout logs — no explicit canary or model version change during that window. However, an automated kernel selection job triggered a heuristic recompile on the dedicated pool servicing FastRetail at 08:41 PST (deployed to a subset of hosts). The hosts that received the new kernel experienced degraded L2 cache behavior for large-context batches; we saw token-processing slowdowns and a downstream increase in request timeouts on long prompts.

I’m attaching the initial metrics export. I’ve started a rollback of the kernel patches on the affected hosts.

Rishi
Senior Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime

Attachment: throughput_summary_2027-11-03.csv

---

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@fastretail.com>, FastRetail SRE Team <sre@fastretail.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Nov 2027 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Production latency spike and errors impacting checkout - immediate attention

Daniel — we’ve pushed a routing rule to pin FastRetail traffic to the previous kernel set and version. Early signs: p95 is trending down (now ~720ms), error rate decreasing. We’ll keep this pinned until Rishi confirms full host remediation.

Action items (initial):
- Rishi: complete rollback and confirm host health (ETA 2h).
- Grace: run a 30m smoke with checkout-heavy load and surface any residual KV-cache regressions (ETA 3h).
- Markus: exec readout + ask for temporary SLA credit (if material revenue impact).

Kim
Director, Support & Customer Ops

---

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Daniel Park <daniel.park@fastretail.com>
Date: Thu, 04 Nov 2027 12:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-incident: validation run and corrective plan

All — completed the smoke run. Findings:
- Throughput and p95 returned to expected baselines after rollback; no functional regressions seen in token outputs for the checkout prompts we used.
- Discovered one host where the fallback cache warm-up was slower (likely due to KV eviction thresholds being too aggressive during the spike).

Proposed corrective actions:
1) Permanently exclude automatic kernel recompile from the dedicated pool serving FastRetail until we complete an A/B validation matrix (owner: Rishi, ETA: 2 weeks).
2) Tweak KV eviction thresholds for checkout-weighted workloads and roll in a staged fashion (owner: Grace + Runtime, ETA: 1 week for canary, 3 weeks full ramp).
3) Provide FastRetail with a 10% SLA credit for the impacted hour and a joint post-incident review (owner: Markus, Kimberly).

I’ll attach the smoke run timeline and graphs to the RCA.

Grace
Senior Reliability Engineer
Attachment: slo-breach-timeline.png

---

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@fastretail.com>, Ava Lin <ava.lin@fastretail.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 06 Nov 2027 16:42:00 -0800
Subject: FastRetail incident: RCA delivered, corrective plan, and next steps

Team / FastRetail execs —

Thanks to the fast triage from both sides. Short executive summary and commitments:

What happened (TL;DR): automated kernel selection triggered a heuristic recompile on a subset of dedicated hosts at ~08:41 PST, which caused degraded low-level cache characteristics for large-context workloads. That led to increased per-token processing time, producing higher tail latency and a spike in 5xxs for the checkout route.

Impact: ~1 hour of elevated p95 and an approximate 6% uplift in failed checkouts for a subset of customers routed to the affected hosts. Estimated incremental revenue impact in that hour: FastRetail estimate attached in Drive link.

Corrective actions and ownership:
- Immediate: pinned FastRetail to previous kernel set (Kimberly) — COMPLETE.
- Remediation: rollback applied to affected hosts (Rishi) — COMPLETE.
- Medium-term: disable automated kernel recompile in the FastRetail pool until a validation matrix is in place (Rishi) — OWNER, ETA 2027-11-20.
- Tuning: KV eviction thresholds adjusted and staged rollout (Grace + Runtime) — OWNER, canary 2027-11-10, full 2027-11-28.
- Customer remediation: 10% credit applied for impacted hour and joint post-incident review scheduled (Markus/Kimberly) — ACTION: Kimberly to confirm credit by 2027-11-08.

Deliverables:
- RCA doc (draft) attached. Final RCAs and the metric packs will be uploaded to the shared Drive.
- SUP-4821 created for follow-through tracking (link below).

Next check-in: 2027-11-10 10:00 PST for canary validation status. Markus will run a brief executive readout if material regressions remain.

Daniel — apologies for the impact. We value FastRetail’s partnership and will make this right.

Regards,
Markus Klein
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: fastretail_rca_draft_v1.pdf
